judged_text: The reschedule cancellation email drops the previous fallback chain entirely: the old code (already buggy with a duplicated expression) never fell back to the user's destinationCalendar, and the new code likewise ignores user.destinationCalendar, sending an empty array when the booking has none. Organizers whose bookings lack a booking-level destinationCalendar (relying on their user-level destinationCalendar) receive cancellation emails whose BrokenIntegrationEmail/calendar rendering takes the 'calendar' default branch instead of naming their connected calendar; users get a degraded but non-crashing email, only in the requestReschedule flow.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/requestReschedule.handler.ts`, the new logic sets `destinationCalendar` to `[bookingToReschedule.destinationCalendar]` or `[]` and never falls back to `bookingToReschedule.user?.destinationCalendar` (unlike many other handlers in this diff that explicitly fall back to the user’s destination calendar). This means when the booking-level destination calendar is absent, downstream code (e.g., `BrokenIntegrationEmail` now destructures `calEvent.destinationCalendar ?? []`) will have no calendar integration info and will take the default "calendar" branch. The finding’s phrasing about “dropping the previous fallback chain” is off (there wasn’t one), but the missing user fallback in the updated code is real and can degrade behavior in the requestReschedule flow.
